source.title: Stop memorizing: A data-dependent regularization framework for intrinsic pattern learning
source.authors: Wei Zhu; Qiang Qiu; Bao Wang; Jianfeng Lu; G. Sapiro; I. Daubechies

record.file_problem: not stated; supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports that conventional networks fit random labels and Gaussian-noise inputs, while its OLE-GRSVNet variant does not; it also compares their accuracy on real labels. This refines the claim by showing the outcome depends on the regularization framework.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports real-label test accuracies in Table 1, but those are not separately rowed: the table contrasts them with random-label training accuracy, and the random-label rows directly capture the claim’s memorization test. Section 4 describes the Gaussian-noise comparison in Figure 2 without exact values. Results cited from Zhang et al. and Arpit et al. are not treated as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The conventional-network controls directly repeat random-label and Gaussian-noise fitting experiments using SGD and training accuracy. The proposed OLE-GRSVNet changes the objective and classifier, so its failures do not contradict versions restricted to standard networks or the named conventional regularizers.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors interpret OLE-GRSVNet's failure to memorize random labels or inputs as reduced memorizing capacity and intrinsic-pattern learning. Their claim of better real-label generalization has one Table 1 exception: CIFAR+ VGG-19 scores 91.65%, versus 91.67% for softmax+OLE. They leave open whether greater capacity or a different optimization outcome could permit memorization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an OLE-GRSVNet data-dependent geometry and self-validation objective rather than the original conventional-network random-label fitting setup; also compares softmax, weight decay and softmax+OLE baselines.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome changes with the regularization/training framework: conventional softmax, weight decay and softmax+OLE fit random labels, while OLE-GRSVNet remains near chance. The OLE-GRSVNet experiments use cross-validated λ values by dataset/model; no sensitivity sweep is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: OLE-GRSVNet remains near chance on random labels and refuses to fit Gaussian-noise inputs, including synthetic MLPs up to 100 layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Replacing the conventional softmax objective and classifier with geometry-consistent self-validation can prevent random-data memorization in the tested networks.

record.peer_reviewed: SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science
record.problems: Random-label test accuracy is omitted from Table 1 (the paper says it is close to 10%). The synthetic MLP and Gaussian-noise results are plotted without uncertainty estimates. The random-label experiments report means over five trials, but no variability statistics.
record.rows_left_out: Real-label test accuracy cells in Table 1 are not separately rowed to keep the extraction focused on random-label fit; Table 1 reports them alongside each architecture’s random-label training accuracy. Figure 2 plots training and test curves for random labels and Gaussian-noise inputs without exact stated values; the Gaussian-noise conditions are retained as figure-only rows R33–R36. No other eligible result rows were omitted.

untested.parts: Section 4 states unchanged hyperparameters, but Section 6 uses 800 random-label epochs versus 100–400 true-label epochs and schedules learning-rate reductions relative to total epochs. A fully identical training schedule is therefore not established throughout. Synthetic test performance is unreported.
No measured time-to-convergence comparison or corruption-fraction sweep. Allocated training budgets do not establish the time required to fit.
Shuffled pixels and independently permuted pixels are not tested.
No intermediate label-corruption fractions or test-error degradation sweep.
Dropout is not tested. Removal of all named regularizers is not systematically isolated; real-label baseline comparisons are reported but explicitly omitted from the extracted rows.
No measurement separating early pattern learning from later noise memorization; Arpit et al. is discussed as prior work.

missing.what: A combined conventional-regularization experiment still perfectly memorizes random labels: weight decay, OLE, batch normalization and augmentation with learning rate increased to 0.1; true-label CIFAR test accuracy is 91.02%. Architecture is not specified in this passage.

record.verdict_notes: OLE-GRSVNet's outcomes do not challenge the literal versions: V1 specifies standard networks, V3 refers to those same networks, and V5 names conventional regularizers. For excluded rows, cannot_determine denotes inability to adjudicate those versions, not uncertainty about the reported accuracy. No original-source exclusion applies.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests random labels on SVHN, MNIST and CIFAR datasets with the stated VGG baselines, plus a synthetic MLP experiment. It does not test every standard architecture or training hyperparameter. Test error at chance is stated in the text, but exact test accuracies for random labels are omitted.
No comparison of time or convergence speed against true-label training, nor sweep over corrupted-label fractions.
Tests Gaussian-noise inputs on SVHN, but not shuffled pixels or independently permuted pixels.
No sweep over fractions of corrupted labels or measurement of smooth test-error degradation.

Tests whether conventional weight decay and softmax+OLE still permit random-label fitting. Does not test dropout, removal of regularizers, or whether removing them alone harms true-label generalization.
No measurement of learning order or comparison of real-label pattern learning with later memorization.
